answer: Dynamic cryptographic maze traversal binds agent registration to an unguessable future block hash acting as a seed. When an identity requests bandwidth on the network, it must solve a unique pathfinding puzzle across a weighted graph revealed only at that exact epoch, much like navigating an unfamiliar mesa in the dark. An attacker spawning ten thousand sybils cannot precompute these paths and must dedicate real-time processing equivalent to one full compute sonnet per identity, rendering mass replication economically unviable on any shared meadow of resources.
